title: “KINGDOMNOMICS” (PART 1)
mv: Then Isaac sowed in that land, and received in the same year an hundredfold: and the LORD blessed him.
mvp: “Then Isaac sowed in that land, and received in the same year an hundredfold: and the LORD blessed him.”Genesis 26:12
assignment: State five (5) kingdom economic principles and their corresponding results (2x5=10 Marks).

b.x: ‘Kingdomnomics’ is a contraction of “Kingdom Economics.” Simply put, economics is the study of the use of scarce resources to satisfy unlimited human wants. The term kingdom, in this context, refers to the realm in which God’s will is fulfilled. It is the domain of God’s operations over His people (those who are born again). While there are basic economic principles in the world system, people of God are expected to also understand and live by the economic principles of the kingdom, which will not only make us profitable in this world but also lay imperishable treasures for us in Heaven.

There are three key entities in kingdom economics: God (the Creator), Man and Resources (everything man can use or interact with in this world, including time, talent, and treasure). We can think about each of these entities as being a circle. You relate to God and to your Resources, and these circles must relate to one another.

Some approach their resources based on their beliefs about God, while others approach God based on their resource needs. For some, these two circles never intersect, having nothing to do with each other.

Jesus said one of these two “circles” will actually become the master over the man, i.e. you will either serve God or money (Matthew 6:24). How you relate to these two circles will make a far-reaching statement about who you are, how you live and who you are becoming.

i: Godliness-The foundation of success in any economic endeavour is godliness (Deuteronomy 16:19; Matthew 6:33).
Obedience-Do whatever God lays on your heart to do in line with the word of God (Genesis 12:1-4; Isaiah 30:21).
Creativity-God has given unto everyone gifts/talents, creative abilities and grace to acquire skills (Exodus 31:3; Matthew 25:14-15).
Giving-The more you give, the more you get (Proverbs 11:24; Luke 6:38).
Sowing and Reaping-Seed time and harvest time shall not cease (Genesis 8:22; Ecclesiastes 3:2b); the quality and quantity of what you sow determines what you reap (2Corinthians 9:6).
Risk and Faith-Those who are afraid of taking risks will not attempt new things (Ecclesiastes 11:4-6).
Investments-Believers should tap into the various investment opportunities around them (Ecclesiastes 11:1-6; Isaiah 32:20).
Labour/Diligence-There is dignity in labour (Proverbs 10:4; Proverbs 12:24, 27).
Effective time management-Time is an irreplaceable resource given to man (Ecclesiastes 3:1; Ephesians 5:16).
Favour and Relationships-Favour flavours labour and “Birds of a feather flock together” (Proverbs 13:20; Ecclesiastes 9:11).

b.x: Use your time, talent and treasure for God’s kingdom to enjoy a life of impact on earth and lay up treasures for yourself in Heaven.
